title: Projects on the streamlined pathway must still meet national environmental standards, which did not exist under the old Act
oneLiner: The counter to the effects claim: the fast route has a floor the slow one never had.
body: The old Act had no binding standards; decisions rested on ministerial judgement against broad objects. The reforms create National Environmental Standards, with the first four commencing from August 2026, and a project can use the streamlined pathway only where it is consistent with them. The national-interest exemption is the one route that can bypass them.
contextBackground: Whether the standards are strong enough is argued separately; that they exist and bind the streamlined route is not.
contextDisagreement: Critics note the standards were still in draft when the pathway was legislated and that the Senate committee asked for revised drafts and clearer benchmarks.

otherClaim.title: The streamlined pathway, bioregional plans and the national-interest exemption could let large-scale land clearing, critical-minerals mines and badly sited renewable projects through with less scrutiny than before

claimItself.title: The streamlined pathway, bioregional plans and the national-interest exemption could let large-scale land clearing, critical-minerals mines and badly sited renewable projects through with less scrutiny than before
claimItself.oneLiner: What kinds of projects the new system could pass: the question most readers actually want answered.
claimItself.body: The reforms create three faster routes: a streamlined assessment for projects that meet the standards, bioregional plans under which actions consistent with the plan need no project-level federal assessment, and the national-interest exemption. Fossil fuel projects are barred from all three. The Environmental Defenders Office warns the remaining routes lack guardrails for large-scale vegetation clearing, critical-mineral mining and renewable energy in unsuitable locations. The claims beneath this one take each project type in turn.
